history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 456 ('Sri Siddharoodha Math', Hubli) - same math, separate CSV row. A monastic institution (math), not a conventional temple, built around the samadhi of the Advaita saint Shri Siddharoodha Swami (born 26 March 1836 at Chalakapura, Bidar district; took samadhi 21 August 1929 at Hubballi). The math propagates his Advaita teaching of universal brotherhood, equality, and selfless service; the complex houses a marble statue of the Swami and runs charitable activities including daily annadana (free meals). Notable visitors included Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1919) and Mahatma Gandhi (1924). The annual car festival is held on Maha Shivaratri. It is located in Srinivas Nagar, Old Hubli, and is regarded as a holy centre of the Hubli-Dharwad region.

town_description: Hubballi (Hubli), twin city of Dharwad, is the commercial and transport hub of North Karnataka and its largest city by population. Once a 12th-century trading post under the Chalukyas, it is today a major railway and industrial centre. Srinivas Nagar in Old Hubli hosts the Siddharoodha Math, the samadhi shrine of the Advaita saint Siddharoodha Swami.

travel.road: Srinivas Nagar, Old Hubli (Karwar Road side), ~4 km from Hubli Junction station; parking can be tight during festivals
